annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 410 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "letter" on page 410 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. During this Age of Men phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net
